os-eol-access.statement: The OS End of Life dashboard is created from a template at Explore > Dashboards > Template Gallery > OS End of Life, with summary tiles, charts and tables on EOL and EOS status.

quotes: To create an OS EOL dashboard from a preconfigured template, go to Explore > Dashboards > Template Gallery > OS End of Life.
The dashboard includes summary tiles, charts, and tables that provides details of the EOL and EOS status of OS assets.

os-eol-tiles.statement: The OS End of Life dashboard Top Assets tiles are: Total Active Assets in EOL, Assets Reaching EOL in the Next 6 Months, Total Active Assets in EOS and Assets Reaching EOS in the Next 6 Months.

quotes: The tiles display the total number of assets, including those that are reaching the EOL or EOS date, and the ones that have already reached the EOL or EOS date.
Total Active Assets in EOL
Assets Reaching EOL in the Next 6 Months
Total Active Assets in EOS
Assets Reaching EOS in the Next 6 Months

os-eol-trend.statement: The Assets in EOL Overtime and Assets in EOS Overtime charts default to the last three months, and clicking a date and View Items lists the active OS assets at EOL or EOS for that date.

quotes: The chart shows the historical trend of OS assets that are no longer supported by their vendors.
The chart's default view displays data from the last three months.
Click a date on the timeline, and click View Items to see a detailed list of active OS assets at EOL for that date.
The chart shows the historical trend of active OS assets in EOS.
The chart's default view displays data from the last three months.
Click a date on the timeline, and click View Items to see a detailed list of active OS assets at EOS for that date.

os-eol-top-n.statement: The OS EOL and OS EOS breakdown-by-OS charts list the top 10 operating systems, and the breakdown-by-owner charts the top 5 owners.

quotes: This chart lists the top 10 operating systems with the highest number of assets affected by EOL.
This chart lists the top 10 operating systems with the highest number of assets affected by EOS.
This chart shows the top 5 owners (e.g., EUC team, Enterprise API team) of assets that are currently at EOL and nearing their EOL date within the next 6 months.
This chart shows the top 5 owners of assets that are currently unsupported and nearing their EOS date within the next 6 months

os-eol-asset-type.statement: The OS EOL and OS EOS breakdown-by-asset-type widgets show OS assets currently at EOL/EOS and nearing the date within the next 6 months by asset type (e.g. Windows workstation, Linux).

quotes: View OS assets that are currently at EOL and nearing their EOL date within the next 6 months by asset type (e.g., Windows workstation, Linux).
View OS assets that are currently unsupported and nearing their EOS date within the next 6 months by asset type (e.g., Windows workstation, Linux).

vt-template.statement: The Violation Tickets Dashboard is created from a template at Explore > Dashboards > Template Gallery > Violation Tickets Dashboard, and breaks tickets down by severity, time and assignee.

quotes: To create this dashboard from a template, go to Explore > Dashboards > Template Gallery > Violation Tickets Dashboard.
The charts and tables provide a detailed breakdown of violation tickets categorized by severity, time, and assignee.

vt-severity-pie.statement: The Open Violation Tickets By Severity pie chart shows open tickets by severity: Critical (maroon), High (red), Medium (orange) and Low (yellow), with a legend giving each category name, count and percentage of total ticket volume.

quotes: Open Violation Tickets By Severity
The pie chart summarizes open violation tickets based on their severity level.
The legend provides details for each category, including the category name, the count of open violation tickets, and the relative percentage of the total ticket volume.
Critical (maroon): The total open violation tickets with the highest risk level.
High (red): The total open violation tickets with significant risk.
Medium (orange): The total open violation tickets with moderate risk.
Low (yellow): The total open violation tickets with low risk.

vt-trend-charts.statement: The Open Violation Tickets Over Time line chart shows the trend of open tickets and Open Violation Tickets Progress Over Time tracks open tickets by severity; clicking a date and View Items lists the open tickets for that date (and severity for the progress chart).

quotes: Open Violation Tickets Over Time
Open Violation Tickets Progress Over Time
The time-series line chart provides a historical overview of open violation tickets
The multi-series line chart tracks the history of open violation tickets by severity level.
Click a date on the timeline, and click View Items to see a detailed list of all open violation tickets for the specific date.
Click a date on the timeline, and click View Items to see a detailed list of all open violation tickets for the specific date and severity level.

vt-remediation-assignee.statement: The Remediation Percentage by Assignee table gives a month-over-month comparison listing the individuals or teams responsible, their open versus closed violation tickets and the rate of ticket closure.

quotes: Remediation Percentage by Assignee
The table provides a month-over-month performance comparison of how teams and individuals resolve violation tickets.
the number of open versus closed violation tickets assigned to them, and the rate of ticket closure.

tc-access-purpose.statement: The Tool Coverage and Gap dashboard is reached in the Agentic Security Operations Platform at Assets > Coverage And Gap and shows asset discovery across integrated asset sources, to identify coverage gaps and overlaps.

quotes: To access the dashboard in the Agentic Security Operations Platform, go to Assets > Coverage And Gap.
You can identify coverage gaps, compare asset discovery between sources, and understand where multiple sources detect the same assets.
Source Name: The integrated asset source such as ITDR Identity AD Computer

tc-find-gap.statement: The Find Coverage Gap widget lists assets not discovered by a selected asset source in a specified time period, taking an Asset source and a Time range entered as a number of days.

quotes: Find Coverage Gap
This widget displays assets that were not discovered by the selected asset source during a specified time period.
Asset source: Select the asset source to evaluate.
Time range: Enter the number of days to analyze asset discovery.

tc-overlaps.statement: The Explore Coverage Overlaps widget compares asset discovery across up to three asset sources.

quotes: Explore Coverage Overlaps
This widget displays and compares asset discovery across multiple asset sources.
Add up to three asset sources to compare using one of the following methods:

tc-asset-coverage.statement: The Asset Coverage table gives for each integrated source its Total Assets, split into a Unique bar (assets discovered only by that source) and an Overlap bar (assets discovered by more than one source).

quotes: Asset Coverage
This table shows a summary of the number of assets discovered by each integrated source, and whether the assets are unique to that source or shared with other sources.
Total Assets: The total number of assets discovered by the source.
Unique bar: Assets discovered only by the selected asset source.
Overlap bar: Assets that were discovered by more than one asset source.

asset-source-list.title: Which asset sources the Tool Coverage and Gap dashboard offers
asset-source-list.detail: The dashboard page shows asset source names only as examples; the full list of selectable sources is not captured.

vt-severity-count.summary: The Violation Tickets dashboard page says the Open Violation Tickets Progress Over Time chart tracks three severity levels, then lists four.

quotes: The chart tracks three distinct severity levels, each represented by a color-coded line.

positions.says: The chart tracks three distinct severity levels.

quotes: Critical (maroon): Open violation tickets with the highest risk level.
High (red): Open violation tickets with significant risk.
Medium (orange): Open violation tickets with moderate risk.
Low (yellow): Open violation tickets with low risk.

positions.says: The page lists four risk levels on the chart: Critical, High, Medium and Low.

vt-severity-count.impact: The page does not say whether the chart draws three or four lines, or which level is not drawn.
